narrative.overview:
The table is set like a premium printed deck: two inks (ink-navy and court-card vermilion), engraved line (brass hairlines, a guilloche rosette in the felt, the card-back lattice reused as the pot medallion), and index typography (a condensed face for every number and label). It refuses the category default of flat neon-green felt with white plates and yellow bubbles, and equally the navy-and-gold casino glow. Depth is printed, not glowed: double rules inset into surfaces, soft offset shadows under cards and plates, no halos.

The product is a training table played under a 30-second clock, so the system is built for reading at a glance. Everything neutral comes from one tinted navy ramp. One loud ink, vermilion, says "act here": the seat to act, the raise button, the timer's last quarter, the all-in stamp, errors. Everything on the table is sized in em of the stage, so the whole table scales as one print; chrome uses a fixed seven-step type scale.

The memorable moment is the pot printed inside a card-back medallion at table center, with the acting seat ringed in vermilion.
keyCharacteristics: One 11-step tinted ink ramp for every neutral; semantic aliases (page, panel, line, text) are what components use.
Vermilion is the single loud ink; brass is the quiet one (hairlines, dealer disc, winner rule, focus ring).
Ivory card stock for playing cards, seat plates and action stamps; nothing else is ivory fill.
Condensed index face (Barlow Condensed, tabular lining numerals) for numbers and labels; Manrope for prose.
Seat state vocabulary is fixed: to-act (vermilion ring, timer, lifts), waiting (ivory), folded (sunk one ink step), all-in (vermilion stamp), winner (brass rule and payout).
Dark only (color-scheme: dark); no light theme exists.

rules.name: The One Loud Ink Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks action and consequence: whose turn, what raises, what is wrong. It is not decoration and it is not a brand wash; on a quiet screen it should appear on one or two things.

rules.name: The Ink Ramp Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a grey. Every neutral is a step of the ink ramp or a semantic alias of one; a new surface picks the nearest step.

rules.name: The Stock Rule
rules.body: Ivory fill belongs to things that are printed paper: playing cards, seat plates, action stamps (and the hand-result mini cards). Ivory otherwise appears only as text on vermilion and as the slider thumb.

rules.name: The State-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Amber and signal green appear only where the state itself is the message, never as accents.

rules.name: The Index Face Rule
rules.body: Every number and every label is font-index. Prose is font-sans. A figure in the prose face is a defect.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Use a text-* step; do not write text-[13px]. The two exceptions (kbd, input) are the whole list. Reading-size floor: 11px.

rules.name: The Merge Rule
rules.body: src/lib/utils.ts registers every type, tracking and spacing token with tailwind-merge. A new token must be added there too, or cn('text-text-2', 'text-body') silently drops the color class.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: The table is one print scaled by one number. Never position a table element in px or give it its own font-size outside the metrics in seat-layout.ts.

rules.name: The Dock Rule
rules.body: Anything the hero must act on or read between hands (actions, sizing, status, the result) lives in the dock. The felt shows the game; the dock shows the decision.

rules.name: The No Halo Rule
rules.body: No blurred colored glow, ever. State is carried by a ring, a rule, a lift, or a one-step ink change.

rules.name: The Engraved Rule
rules.body: A surface that should feel printed gets a double rule painted with inset box-shadow, which never changes the box size.

dos: Do take every neutral from the ink ramp through the semantic aliases (bg-panel, border-line, text-text-2).
Do set every number and label in font-index / label-index, and every sentence in font-sans.
Do use a text-* scale step and a spacing role (p-gutter, gap-snug); register any new token in src/lib/utils.ts.
Do keep the seat state vocabulary exact: vermilion ring and lift for to-act, sunk ivory-shade for folded, vermilion stamp for all-in, brass rule and payout for winner.
Do size every table element in em of the stage and place it in percent of the box via seat-layout.ts; add data-layout-box to anything new on the table or in the chrome.
Do keep text at 11px or more, and body text at 4.5:1 or better on its ground.
Do put decisions and the hand result in the dock, and keep keyboard parity: every action has a hotkey.
Do keep depth to offset-and-blur shadows and inset double rules.
donts: Don't add flat neon-green felt, white plates, yellow chip bubbles, or navy-and-gold casino glow (the confirmed category defaults this system refuses).
Don't use vermilion as decoration or a second accent color; don't add a new hue for a new feature.
Don't put a blurred colored glow or halo on any state.
Don't render Unicode suit glyphs; use SuitIcon.
Don't use arbitrary pixel type (text-[13px]) or half-step spacing (p-1.5, px-2.5, px-3.5).
Don't lay a modal, toast, or floating banner over the felt; the felt is for the game.
Don't let the stage reserve space for the dock, or position table elements in px.
Don't use block as a spacing role; the 32px step is major.
